sentence: This project studies how a transcription factor helps regulatory T cells hold back the immune response against tumors in mice and humans.
This project tries to find out what causes cancer and cancer-related behavior, and works to prevent and control cancer.
This project builds a computer program to find out how high blood sugar and fat together change blood vessels and lead to heart disease.
This project tests treatments made from elastin-like polypeptides for gland and body-wide inflammation in an autoimmune disease, using mice.
This project builds technology to find drugs that control how calcium moves in skeletal muscle.
This project tries to find out where uremic toxins come from and how the gut microbiome adds to them in children with kidney failure.
This project brings together cancer research and clinical work to improve cancer therapy.
This project studies what raises the risk of clonal hematopoiesis and how it relates to age-related diseases in people with exceptional longevity.
This project studies how damaged tissue in the Drosophila testis senses damage and then makes missing stem cells to regenerate.
This project tries to find out how hearing loss in one ear changes hearing and balance in the other, intact inner ear, using mice.
This project studies how mutations in the myelin protein zero gene cause neuropathy and tests a gene therapy in mice.
This project brings together researchers to discuss how genetic and epigenetic mechanisms shape brain development.
This project supports research on how brain development, behavior and cognition are affected in people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
This project tries to find out which genes control bile duct development and tests an approach in a mouse model.
This project studies how a high fat diet causes inflammation in the hypothalamus, focusing on a cell type called tanycytes.
This project describes the human virome, the collection of all viruses found inside and on the human body, using genomic technologies and computational analyses.
This project builds a one-time gene therapy that lowers the prion protein to treat, prevent or delay prion disease, testing it in mice.
This project tries to find out whether an enzyme that changes lipids can be a drug target in Ewing sarcoma, an aggressive pediatric cancer.
This project studies whether certain cancer patients are more likely to have bad reactions to immune checkpoint inhibitors, and which social factors are involved.
This project screens natural products from marine microbes to find pain medicines that are not addictive, using sensory cell cultures and microelectrode arrays.
